answers.value: People who want to build a daily habit have nowhere simple and private to track it. Existing apps are bloated, ad-ridden, or sell your data. Someone trying to meditate or run every morning is worse off because the friction of heavy tools makes them quit before the habit sticks.

response.mission: Habit Tracker gives one person a simple, private place to build a daily habit — no ads, no accounts, no data harvesting — so the tool never becomes the reason they quit.

values.title: Stay true to your users
values.rationale: Every feature serves the person building a habit, not a growth metric.

values.title: Ship before perfect
values.rationale: A working daily streak beats a beautiful unfinished dashboard.

values.title: Document it or it doesn't exist
values.rationale: If a behaviour is not written down, the next change will break it.

values.title: Keep it private by default
values.rationale: A habit is personal; data stays on the user's device unless they ask otherwise.

values.title: Reduce friction relentlessly
values.rationale: Every extra tap is a reason to skip a day.

aiLaws: Never add a dependency without asking first.
Keep user data local unless the user explicitly opts in to sync.
Fail loudly and visibly; never swallow an error.
Prefer the simplest implementation that satisfies the acceptance criteria.
